rules.statement: A failed or timed-out lookup returns no groups for that request (access denied or a retryable error) and leaves no cache entry.
rules.acceptance: A failing fake denies the request, and the next request retries the directory.

rules.title: Writes read groups live
rules.statement: Any request that changes data resolves the caller's groups from the directory, bypassing the cache. Reads tolerate the TTL.
rules.acceptance: Remove a user from the fake's group, then a write is refused at once while a read may still pass inside the TTL.

rules.title: In-app membership changes invalidate the cache
rules.statement: When the app itself adds or removes a member, it drops the affected users' cache entries in the same request.
rules.acceptance: After an in-app grant the next request for that user misses the cache.

rules.title: Cache the managed identity token for the directory
rules.statement: The API gets its directory token from its managed identity and reuses it until shortly before expiry, never per lookup.
rules.acceptance: Two lookups in a row request one token.

rules.title: Drop the token on a 401
rules.statement: A 401 from the directory clears the cached token, and the lookup retries once with a fresh one.
rules.acceptance: A fake that answers 401 once is retried once with a new token.

rules.title: Send Access-Control-Max-Age 7200
rules.statement: Preflight responses carry the browser cap (7200 seconds) so a browser asks once per two hours, not once per call.
rules.acceptance: An OPTIONS request from a listed origin returns Access-Control-Max-Age 7200.

rules.title: Keep an origin guard behind CORS
rules.statement: The API refuses writes and preflighted requests whose Origin is not on the list, independent of the CORS headers.
rules.acceptance: A write with an unlisted Origin returns 403 even when no preflight happened.

rules.title: Send Server-Timing marks to allowlisted origins
rules.statement: Each response carries marks for the costly steps (token check, group lookup with hit, miss or shared, permission check), with Timing-Allow-Origin set, only when the request Origin is on the list.
rules.acceptance: A listed origin gets Server-Timing and Timing-Allow-Origin, an unlisted one gets neither.

rules.title: One structured log line per request, nothing personal
rules.statement: The line holds method, route template, status, duration and the timing marks. It never holds the URL, query string, token, user name, email or object id.
rules.acceptance: A request with a query string and a bearer token logs one line that contains neither.

rules.title: Route names come only from declared route templates
rules.statement: The route name is read from the router's declared templates (walk the router definitions at startup), never built from the request path or the mount path values. A request that matches no declared template is named -.
rules.acceptance: Requests with ids, emails and unknown paths produce only declared templates or -.

rules.title: Health probes are not sent
rules.statement: Requests to the health endpoint are not recorded as telemetry.
rules.acceptance: A health request produces no telemetry item.

rules.title: Keyless ingestion
rules.statement: Local (key) auth is off on the telemetry resource. The API sends with its managed identity, which holds only the metrics publisher role on that resource.
rules.acceptance: The resource has local auth disabled and the identity holds only the publisher role.

rules.title: One telemetry component per API with a daily cap, and no stray alert mail
rules.statement: Each API reports to its own component with a daily ingestion cap. The anomaly alert rule the platform creates on its own is disabled or kept from mailing a shared action group.
rules.acceptance: Every component has a cap and no auto-created rule targets a shared group.

rules.title: Telemetry never blocks startup and flushes on SIGTERM
rules.statement: The exporter starts after the server listens, its failure is logged and ignored, and a SIGTERM handler flushes with a short timeout before exit.
rules.acceptance: With an unreachable endpoint the server still answers, and SIGTERM exits within the timeout.

rules.title: Prefer the lightweight exporter on small plans
rules.statement: Use a plain trace SDK with the vendor exporter, not the vendor's all-in-one distribution.
rules.acceptance: The API's dependencies hold the exporter, not the distribution.

rules.title: One package for the runtime middleware, consumed by every API
rules.statement: Group caching, the directory token, the origin guard, Server-Timing, the request log and telemetry route naming live in one shared package that every API imports.
rules.acceptance: No API carries its own copy of these middlewares.

rules.title: The shared package has no runtime dependencies
rules.statement: It uses only the platform's standard library and what the consuming API already passes in.
rules.acceptance: A check in the consumer's CI asserts the package manifest lists no runtime dependencies.

rules.title: Validate the bearer token completely
rules.statement: The shared bearer check verifies signature (pinned algorithm allowlist), issuer, audience, expiry and not-before, refreshes signing keys on an unknown key id at most once per interval, and never accepts a token after a failed refresh.
rules.acceptance: Tokens with a wrong algorithm, issuer, audience, signature or expiry each return 401.

rules.title: The dev identity is for development and test only
rules.statement: DEV_BYPASS_AUTH is honoured only when the environment is development or test, and a boot preflight refuses any other environment while the bypass or a dev user is set.
rules.acceptance: A start with the bypass set in staging, unset or production exits non-zero before listening.

rules.title: Look up only referenced groups, in batches, with a generation guard
rules.statement: The resolver asks only about the groups the apps reference, sends at most 20 ids per call with at most 4 calls in flight, falls back to one id per call on a 400, retries a 429 once, and never writes a lookup that started before an invalidation into the cache.
rules.acceptance: A test proves the referenced-only lookup, the batch and concurrency bounds, the 400 and 429 handling and that an invalidation during a lookup leaves the cache empty.

rules.title: CORS lives in the app only
rules.statement: The hosting platform CORS setting stays empty for every API; the app CORS layer and origin guard decide origins.
rules.acceptance: repo check RC005 reports no platform CORS origin list in hosting or infrastructure config.

rules.title: Retry telemetry exports through a short outage
rules.statement: A failed export is retried after 2, 5 and 10 seconds and unsent spans wait in a bounded buffer of 2,000; a full buffer drops the oldest and logs once per outage.
rules.acceptance: With a fake collector down for 8 seconds no span is lost; past the buffer it holds 2,000 spans and logs one warning.

rules.title: Fixed bearer rules and a development-only dev identity
rules.statement: Bearer tokens use one signing algorithm (RS256), both issuer versions, the audience as the union of the API ids, signing keys cached 10 minutes with at most 10 key fetches a minute. A dev identity exists only when the environment is exactly development or test.
rules.acceptance: A token signed with another algorithm, a wrong audience and an unknown key id flood each fail; the dev identity is refused when the environment is unset or staging.

rules.title: One canonical boot sequence
rules.statement: The app initializes the auth library, handles the redirect response, sets the active account, then renders. The stored return target is routed in-app (MSAL navigateToLoginRequestUrl: false), never by a second full page load.
rules.acceptance: A simulated sign-in return renders the target route with one boot and no extra navigation.

rules.title: One boot module for every app
rules.statement: The boot sequence lives in the shared client package (section 5), not in each app.
rules.acceptance: repo check RC009 reports the auth redirect handled in at most one non-test source file.

rules.title: Never depend on hidden-iframe renewal when the origin denies framing
rules.statement: When the app origin sends X-Frame-Options DENY (or a frame-ancestors policy that blocks itself), silent renewal uses the refresh token only (MSAL cache lookup policy refresh-token-only), never the hidden iframe fallback.
rules.acceptance: With an expired access token and a valid refresh token, renewal succeeds with no iframe created.

rules.title: Iframe timeouts mean interaction required
rules.statement: Timeout errors from the silent path (MSAL monitor_window_timeout and its relatives) are treated as interaction required, so the user is sent to sign in once.
rules.acceptance: A silent call that fails with a timeout code starts one interactive sign-in.

rules.title: Only real session expiry redirects
rules.statement: Interaction required is decided by the session-expiry codes (expired or missing session, refresh token expired). Consent and conditional access policy errors are shown to the user once and never start a redirect.
rules.acceptance: A consent error renders a message and starts no redirect.

rules.title: Check the loop guard before redirecting
rules.statement: A guard (a counter or timestamp in session storage) is read before every interactive redirect, and a tripped guard shows a sign-in button instead.
rules.acceptance: Two redirects inside the guard window show the button and start no third redirect.

rules.title: Single-flight the interactive redirect
rules.statement: One redirect promise is shared by every caller, and the library's interaction in progress error is treated as "already redirecting".
rules.acceptance: Five concurrent calls that need interaction start one redirect and report no error.

rules.title: Match errors by name and code too
rules.statement: Error checks compare the error name and code as well as instanceof.
rules.acceptance: An error object from a different library copy with the same name and code is classified the same way.

rules.title: The bearer token goes only to the configured API base
rules.statement: The client attaches the token only to paths under the configured base, and rejects absolute URLs, protocol-relative paths, backslashes, path traversal and encoded dot segments.
rules.acceptance: Each rejected form throws before any request leaves, and no token is attached.

rules.title: Identical GETs in flight share one request
rules.statement: A GET for a key that is already in flight returns the same promise.
rules.acceptance: Three concurrent GETs of one path produce one request.

rules.title: Stale-while-revalidate with a per-key TTL
rules.statement: Cached reads return at once and refresh in the background when older than their TTL, and each key may set its own TTL. A poll interval on the page counts as meeting this when every cached read is refreshed at least that often; no cached value lives forever.
rules.acceptance: A stale key returns the cached value and starts one background refresh.

rules.title: Persist only identity reads, and always as stale
rules.statement: Only identity reads (who am I, my permissions) persist to sessionStorage so the shell paints at once on load. They are always treated as stale, and cleared on sign-out and on an account change.
rules.acceptance: A reload paints from storage and refetches, sign-out and an account switch clear it.

rules.title: Invalidate drops in-flight GETs
rules.statement: Invalidating a key also forgets any in-flight GET for it, so the next read starts fresh.
rules.acceptance: A GET in flight during a write is not returned to a caller that reads after the invalidate.

rules.title: A rejected refresh leaves no stuck entry
rules.statement: A failed or superseded request removes its in-flight entry, and a stale rejection never overwrites newer data.
rules.acceptance: After a rejected GET the next read sends a new request.

rules.title: Background polls never navigate
rules.statement: A poll passes its own on-401 handler that throws, so only a user-started call may send the user to sign in.
rules.acceptance: A 401 on a poll throws to the poller and starts no navigation.

rules.title: Polls pause while the tab is hidden
rules.statement: Polling stops on visibility hidden and resumes, with one immediate refresh, when the tab is visible again.
rules.acceptance: No poll fires while the document is hidden.

rules.title: Lazy routes, first page started at boot, the rest prefetched on idle
rules.statement: Every route is a lazy chunk. The route the user landed on starts loading during boot, and the other routes prefetch when the browser is idle.
rules.acceptance: repo check RC019 reports a bundled app with no bundle size budget check (a size-limit or bundlewatch config, or a budget script).

rules.title: Long-lived vendor chunks
rules.statement: The framework and the auth library build into their own named chunks so an app release does not change their hashes.
rules.acceptance: repo check RC018 reports no vite config without manualChunks.

rules.title: Large inline assets become hashed files
rules.statement: Images, fonts and data above a few kilobytes are emitted as hashed files, not inlined into the script.
rules.acceptance: repo check RC020 reports no vite config without assetsInlineLimit.

rules.title: One client package for every app on the origin
rules.statement: Auth boot, token renewal, the API client and polling live in one package that every app imports.
rules.acceptance: repo check RC021 reports no app whose client code builds the bearer header in more than one file.

rules.title: One token cache across apps on the same origin
rules.statement: Apps on one origin share the auth library's cache location and client configuration, so signing in to one signs in to all.
rules.acceptance: After signing in to one app, another app on the origin acquires a token silently.

rules.title: Every app shows the same live strip from one feed endpoint
rules.statement: A health line and platform announcements come from one feed endpoint that requires sign-in and no extra permission, and every app renders them with the shared component.
rules.acceptance: Every app mounts the shared strip against the one feed endpoint.

rules.title: Per-app items are gated by the user's own permissions
rules.statement: The feed adds items for an app only when the caller holds that app's permissions, and each app may add its own items to the strip.
rules.acceptance: A user without an app's permission receives none of its items.

rules.title: An app without a session bounces once, with a validated return target
rules.statement: An app with no session signs in with the current in-app path as the return target, accepted on return only as a same-origin path (single leading slash, no //, backslash, control character, more than 2048 characters or other origin). A rejected target routes to the app home.
rules.acceptance: Each rejected form routes to the app home and a valid deep link returns to itself.

rules.title: An account change clears the old account's state
rules.statement: When the active account changes, cached API data and error state for the old account are cleared and the app re-boots for the new one.
rules.acceptance: Switching account in a second tab clears cached data and the error banner in the first.

rules.title: Pure signal, plain language, no sensitive content
rules.statement: Send only failures and things that need action, in plain words, in first person where the message speaks for the owner, with no AI or tool attribution, no PHI, identifiers or credentials, and never a change to what is sent to other people.
rules.acceptance: A review of a sample of alerts finds none that break the principles.

rules.title: HTML parse mode, no banned characters
rules.statement: Messages use HTML parse mode with only <, > and & escaped, and the formatter strips em and en dashes, curly quotes and other banned characters.
rules.acceptance: The formatter test covers escaping and stripping.

rules.title: Messages follow the standard layout
rules.statement: Every message uses the layout: severity icon and bold headline, time line, plain-language body, next step, collapsed facts and log excerpt, read-only buttons, capped at 4096 characters.
rules.acceptance: The formatter samples render each element and the truncation.

rules.title: Severity levels have fixed icons and sounds
rules.statement: Critical, failure, warning, recovered and info use the documented icon and sound, and recovered is sent only after an earlier alert for the same key.
rules.acceptance: The formatter samples show each level.

rules.title: Alerts are deduplicated per key and recover
rules.statement: The same severity for the same key is suppressed for 15 minutes (critical), 1 hour (failure) or 6 hours (warning, info), and a recovered message is sent only when an alert was open.
rules.acceptance: The formatter tests cover suppression and recovery.

rules.title: Delivery goes direct to the owner and never raises
rules.statement: Send goes by direct Bot API call to the owner chat only, with the token read at runtime and never printed, falling back from rich with buttons to rich to plain text, and a delivery failure never raises into the calling job.
rules.acceptance: A forced failure leaves the calling job exit code unchanged.

rules.title: Scheduled jobs run under the guard
rules.statement: Scheduled jobs run through the guard wrapper, which sends one formatted alert on failure, preserves the exit code and avoids a second plain failure notice.
rules.acceptance: A failing guarded job sends exactly one alert and exits non-zero.

rules.title: Email goes through one renderer behind a CI guard
rules.statement: Every email a tool sends goes through one block renderer: a fixed-width card, callouts without edge bars, a subject naming the change and item, lists capped at 12, public-hostname links and [TEST] self-tests to the sender only. A CI guard fails hand-built email HTML and platform-host links.
rules.acceptance: A fixture with a raw table in an email module and one with a platform-host link each fail the guard.

rules.title: The directory is the source of truth for identity
rules.statement: The identity provider directory owns object id, display name, email and job title. The app stores a cached copy, never a competing one. A fallback copy of the last directory pull is allowed when it is read only if the directory pull fails and is marked stale on screen; the directory pull wins whenever it succeeds and no copy is edited by hand.
rules.acceptance: No write path edits an identity field except the sync.

rules.title: One roster
rules.statement: A single team_members table is the only list of people and every feature links to it by member id, any stable key the directory supplies.
rules.acceptance: No feature table holds its own list of names, and a rename or reorganisation never orphans history.

rules.title: Directory-only adds
rules.statement: New members are added only by picking a user from the directory, and adding is refused when the directory is unavailable.
rules.acceptance: A test shows a free-text add is refused.

rules.title: Never fabricate people from name-only data
rules.statement: A seed, import or migration with only a name does not create a member.
rules.acceptance: A test shows a name-only import creates no member.

rules.title: Nightly sync with confident matching
rules.statement: A scheduled sync matches by object id, then exact email, then exact display name when safe, and an ambiguous match is marked unmatched and changes nothing.
rules.acceptance: Sync tests cover each match tier and the ambiguous case.

rules.title: Safe propagation
rules.statement: A confident match overwrites team_members without blanking fields, linked snapshots are fill-only, and past schedule rows, swap audit and OOF entries are never rewritten.
rules.acceptance: A sync test shows snapshots and past rows unchanged.

rules.title: Test data is synthetic
rules.statement: Fixtures and seeds use made-up people on example.test, never real staff.
rules.acceptance: repo check RC008 reports no fixture email address outside the reserved test domains.

rules.title: One auth model per app type, dev bypass development or test only
rules.statement: An app behind the platform uses platform-level auth; the dev bypass is honoured only in development or test, and a boot preflight refuses a production start while it is set.
rules.acceptance: A start with the bypass set in production, staging or an unset environment exits before listening.

rules.title: One tools manifest drives every navigation surface
rules.statement: A single manifest feeds the hub, sidebars and palette; visibility combines the view permissions, accessPrefixes (never narrower than the server), hiddenWithPermission, visibleTo for scoped grants, and previewFlag for nav items.
rules.acceptance: A tool with hiddenWithPermission is hidden from a caller holding it; a nav item with an unregistered flag is hidden; a caller with only an access-prefix permission reaches the tool.

rules.title: One local gate runs what CI runs
rules.statement: One script (pnpm run verify) runs typecheck, lint, every check guard, the build, the bundle-size check, the tests and the pinned static analysis scan, failing on the first non-zero step.
rules.acceptance: repo check RC016 reports a package with no verify script, or one that does not run each check:* script and each typecheck, lint, build and test script the package defines.

rules.title: One global search, access-filtered, with index health
rules.statement: Global search covers every record the user can see, filters by the record access rules on the server, indexes up to 100,000 characters of file text with a highlighted passage, and reports stale, skipped and broken-link counts from a health endpoint.
rules.acceptance: A search never returns a key the caller cannot read; the health endpoint reports a stale fixture document.

rules.title: Pick one shell shape per product
rules.statement: A product is either several apps on one origin or one shell with many modules; a module inside a shell never signs in on its own or tries a silent sign-in frame.
rules.acceptance: A module with no session bounces to the shell sign-in with no hidden frame.

rules.title: Client-runtime sections apply per shape
rules.statement: Each client-runtime section applies as the shape table says; with platform sign-in there is no browser token, so auth boot, renewal and the token cache do not apply.
rules.acceptance: Review against the table.

rules.title: The registry is generated from manifests
rules.statement: A script generates the module list and one icon map with a fallback from per-module manifests, and CI fails a stale registry.
rules.acceptance: A manifest added without regenerating fails CI; a module with no icon gets the fallback.

rules.title: One route table, standalone or hosted
rules.statement: A module exports one route table, a shared typed descriptor and a host hook; the standalone entry and the shell mount the same table.
rules.acceptance: A manifest test per module keeps manifest and route table aligned.

rules.title: Per-module CSS scope
rules.statement: Module stylesheets are built inside :where([data-module="<id>"]), keyframes are named <id>-<name>, root selectors map onto the module root, and the token sheet loads once.
rules.acceptance: A kit test asserts module rules are prefixed inside :where([data-module=id]) at zero specificity and root selectors map onto the module root, so a module rule matches only its own module.

rules.title: Per-module storage scope
rules.statement: Each module has its own appId so seen versions, dismissed banners and saved filters stay per module.
rules.acceptance: A banner dismissed in one module still shows in another.

rules.title: One accent per mounted module
rules.statement: Each module mounts in the kit AccentProvider with an accent name from the kit accents data.
rules.acceptance: Switching modules switches the accent with no leftovers.

rules.title: Safe return-target bounce
rules.statement: The shell validates the return target and accepts only a same-origin path, rejecting protocol-relative, backslash, control-character, over-2,048-character and other-origin targets.
rules.acceptance: Each rejected shape returns the home route; a plain in-origin path survives.

rules.title: Home is the hub
rules.statement: In a multi-module shell home is the hub; module pages never claim /, and the header Home, the bounce fallback and the palette point there.
rules.acceptance: Review of the route table and header home.

rules.title: One AppShell per module, mounted and routed by id
rules.statement: Each active module gets its own AppShell, a router at /<id>, a remount on switch and rail entries filtered by its own permission check; the switcher uses the Rail brandSlot.
rules.acceptance: Switching modules remounts; a same-origin link into another module does not reload; a hidden rail entry still answers 403 from the server.
